stories.headline: Micron and SK Hynix top $1 trillion as all three memory chipmakers join the club

key_facts.fact: Micron topped a $1 trillion market value for the first time on Tuesday, May 26, as shares jumped 19%, after UBS nearly tripled its price target on the stock from $535 to $1,625.
key_facts.excerpt: Micron topped a $1 trillion market value for the first time on Tuesday as shares popped 19%... The stock surge came as UBS tripled its price target on the stock from $535 to $1,625 a share.

key_facts.fact: UBS cited long-term supply agreements with partially fixed pricing and AI-driven demand; Micron's stock has more than tripled year to date.
key_facts.excerpt: citing long-term agreement opportunities with partially fixed pricing... Micron's stock has more than tripled year to date.

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix jumped more than 12% to a record high on Wednesday, May 27, lifting its market cap to roughly $1.08 trillion and making it the second South Korean company after Samsung to hit $1 trillion.
key_facts.excerpt: SK Hynix crossed a $1 trillion market cap on Wednesday after its stock jumped more than 12% to a record high... pushed the company's total market value to roughly 1,624 trillion won, or $1.08 trillion.

key_facts.fact: With SK Hynix's move, all three of the world's largest memory chipmakers - Samsung, Micron and SK Hynix - now hold trillion-dollar valuations at the same time for the first time.
key_facts.excerpt: The milestone means Samsung Electronics, SK hynix and Micron Technology are now all valued above $1 trillion following a sectorwide surge fueled by AI infrastructure spending.

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix is up more than 248% year to date in 2026 after a 200%+ rally in 2025, and is the third Asian company to reach a $1 trillion valuation, behind Samsung and TSMC.
key_facts.excerpt: SK Hynix stock is up more than 248% year to date in 2026, following a 200%+ rally in 2025... It is now the third Asian company to reach a $1 trillion valuation overall, behind Samsung and TSMC.

key_facts.fact: Samsung Electronics crossed the $1 trillion mark first, on May 6, becoming the first South Korean company to do so.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung Electronics became the first Korean company to surpass a $1 trillion valuation on May 6.

key_facts.fact: The rally is driven by surging demand for high-bandwidth memory (HBM) for AI accelerators and a global memory shortage that has let makers raise prices.
key_facts.excerpt: Driven by explosive demand for high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and expanding AI data center investment, SK hynix surpassed a $1 trillion market capitalization.

stories.headline: Qualcomm strikes deal to supply ByteDance millions of AI data-center chips

key_facts.fact: Qualcomm reached a deal to supply ByteDance with millions of application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs) for AI data centers, per a Bloomberg report on Tuesday, May 26.
key_facts.excerpt: Qualcomm reached a deal with TikTok owner ByteDance to supply chips for AI data centers, Bloomberg News reported on Tuesday... ByteDance is set to procure millions of Qualcomm chips known as application-specific integrated circuits.

key_facts.fact: ByteDance will use the chips to underpin its AI-agent software and is poised to become one of Qualcomm's first major named customers for its AI-focused ASICs.
key_facts.excerpt: to help support the social media company's AI agent software... poised to become one of Qualcomm's first major customers for the AI-focused application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs).

key_facts.fact: Qualcomm shares closed up around 5% on the news, with intraday gains touching above 8%.
key_facts.excerpt: Qualcomm's shares closed up around 5% on the news, with intraday gains touching above 8%.

key_facts.fact: The agreement has two parts: a straight ASIC-supply arrangement, plus a chip-manufacturing-services layer in which Qualcomm helps bring ByteDance's own internally designed chip to volume production.
key_facts.excerpt: The first is a straight ASIC-supply arrangement... The second... is a chip-manufacturing-services layer: Qualcomm will help ByteDance bring an internally designed semiconductor... to volume production.

key_facts.fact: The structure is designed to work around US export controls: Qualcomm's ASICs reportedly sit within the US Commerce Department's computing-performance thresholds, and ByteDance's in-house design is engineered to stay within the same limits.
key_facts.excerpt: The structure matters because it works around US export controls. Qualcomm's ASICs... sit within the legal computing-performance thresholds that the US Commerce Department has set... ByteDance's own in-house design is being engineered to stay inside the same thresholds.

key_facts.fact: The deal is expected to ramp through 2026 and 2027; Qualcomm declined to comment on the specifics.
key_facts.excerpt: Qualcomm declined to comment on the specifics of the ByteDance arrangement. The deal is expected to ramp through 2026 and 2027.

key_facts.fact: ByteDance has reportedly raised its AI-related budget about 25% to roughly 200 billion yuan ($29.4 billion).
key_facts.excerpt: its AI-related budget reportedly rising by around 25% to approximately 200 billion yuan ($29.4 billion).

stories.headline: Nvidia's Huang says it will spend about $150 billion a year in Taiwan, the AI 'epicentre'

key_facts.fact: At a Wednesday, May 27 launch celebration in Taipei for Nvidia's planned Taiwan headquarters, CEO Jensen Huang said the company plans to invest around $150 billion a year in Taiwan, calling it the 'epicentre' of the AI revolution.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia's chief executive said on Wednesday (May 27) the chip company plans to invest around US$150 billion a year in Taiwan, terming it the 'epicentre' of the AI revolution.

key_facts.fact: Huang said spending had risen from $10-15 billion a year in Taiwan four or five years ago to $100 billion now, heading toward $150 billion a year.
key_facts.excerpt: 'Four years ago, five years ago, Nvidia was spending about 10, 15 billion dollars a year in Taiwan. Now we're spending 100, going to 150 billion dollars in Taiwan each year,' CEO Jensen Huang said.

key_facts.fact: The new Taiwan headquarters will break ground this year, aims to be operational in 2030, and is set to employ 4,000 people, in Taipei's Beitou-Shilin Technology Park.
key_facts.excerpt: The project will break ground this year and aims to be operational in 2030... He said Nvidia planned to employ 4,000 people at the new site.

key_facts.fact: Huang called Nvidia's next-generation Vera Rubin platform 'probably the largest product launch in the history of Taiwan'; each system contains nearly 2 million parts built across about 150 Taiwanese supply-chain partners.
key_facts.excerpt: Vera Rubin, Nvidia's next-generation AI platform, which Huang called 'probably the largest product launch in the history of Taiwan'... Each Vera Rubin system contains nearly 2 million parts and is built through 150 ecosystem partners on the island.

key_facts.fact: The $150 billion is an aggregate figure flowing through the existing Taiwanese ecosystem - TSMC fabricates the logic while Foxconn, Quanta and Wistron handle assembly - rather than a discrete new capital plan.
key_facts.excerpt: The $150bn is an aggregate figure flowing through the existing Taiwanese ecosystem, not a discrete capital plan... TSMC fabricates the underlying logic. Foxconn, Quanta, Wistron and others handle assembly.

key_facts.fact: Huang spoke as the head of the world's most valuable company, valued at around $5 trillion, to a Taipei crowd of about 1,000 employees.
key_facts.excerpt: at a launch celebration in Taipei for the US$5 trillion chipmaker's planned Taiwan headquarters... a crowd including his family, around 1,000 employees and Taipei Mayor Chiang Wan-an.

stories.headline: Samsung union ratifies bonus deal, averting a strike at the top memory chipmaker

key_facts.fact: Samsung Electronics union members voted on Wednesday, May 27 to ratify a wage-and-bonus agreement, ending roughly five months of negotiations and averting a strike that threatened the world's top memory chipmaker.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung Electronics and its unions concluded five grueling months of wage negotiations after workers voted to ratify a tentative agreement on Wednesday, averting a strike that had threatened to disrupt the world's top memory chipmaker.

key_facts.fact: Of 65,593 eligible voters, 62,616 cast ballots (95.5% turnout), with 73.7% - 46,142 members - voting in favor.
key_facts.excerpt: 65,593 eligible voters cast ballots, a turnout of 95.5 percent, with 73.7 percent, or 46,142 members, voting in favor of the agreement.

key_facts.fact: The deal pays memory chip employees roughly $400,000 each this year, while colleagues in smartphones and home appliances receive closer to $4,000.
key_facts.excerpt: a package that will pay memory chip employees roughly $400,000 each this year while their colleagues in smartphones and home appliances receive closer to just $4,000.

key_facts.fact: The agreement allocates 10.5% of Samsung's semiconductor division operating profit as stock-based bonuses plus an additional 1.5% in cash, running for 10 years and contingent on hitting operating-profit targets of 200 trillion won ($132 billion) from 2026 to 2028.
key_facts.excerpt: allocates 10.5% of Samsung's semiconductor division operating profit as stock-based bonuses, plus an additional 1.5% in cash. The program runs for 10 years, contingent on the division hitting aggressive annual operating profit targets of 200 trillion won ($132 billion) from 2026 to 2028.

key_facts.fact: The vote follows a last-minute, government-mediated tentative deal struck on May 20 that suspended an 18-day general strike by 48,000 workers set to begin on May 21.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung Electronics and its labor union reached a tentative agreement late Wednesday, about one hour before a planned general strike was set to begin on May 21. The union will suspend the 18-day strike that had been scheduled to run through June 7.

key_facts.fact: The vote exposed divisions: memory chip workers, who make up the majority of the union, benefit far more than consumer-electronics (DX) workers, who had tried unsuccessfully to block the vote in court.
key_facts.excerpt: A South Korean court on Tuesday dismissed an attempt by Samsung Electronics' consumer electronics workers to block ratification... The Suwon District Court rejected the injunction filed by five employees from Samsung's Device eXperience (DX) division.

stories.headline: TeraWulf buys 1+ GW Eastern Kentucky site to expand its AI data-center pipeline

key_facts.fact: TeraWulf announced on May 26 the acquisition of the Muskie Data Campus, a hyperscale HPC development site in Eastern Kentucky, from Industrial Equity Partners.
key_facts.excerpt: TeraWulf Inc... today announced the acquisition of a hyperscale high-performance computing ('HPC') development site strategically located in Eastern Kentucky (the 'Muskie Data Campus')... acquired from Industrial Equity Partners ('IEP').

key_facts.fact: The site is expected to support more than 1 gigawatt of data-center capacity, with the initial 500 MW ramping in the second half of 2028 and a further 500 MW targeted for the second half of 2030.
key_facts.excerpt: expected to support more than 1 gigawatt ('GW') of data center capacity over time. Delivery of the initial 500 megawatts ('MW') is expected to ramp beginning in the second half of 2028, with an additional 500 MW targeted for delivery in the second half of 2030.

key_facts.fact: Kentucky Power, an AEP company, is building a 345 kV substation connected to the existing 765 kV transmission network to supply utility-scale power to the 285-acre campus.
key_facts.excerpt: Kentucky Power is building a 345 kV substation to connect the 285-acre site to a 765 kV transmission network for redundant, utility-scale power.

key_facts.fact: Transmission infrastructure and energy service agreements were executed concurrently with the acquisition.
key_facts.excerpt: Transmission infrastructure and energy service agreements were executed concurrently with the acquisition pursuant to the applicable Industrial General Service tariff structure for large loads.

key_facts.fact: TeraWulf shares rose about 8% in pre-market trading on Tuesday after the announcement; CEO Paul Prager said the binding constraint for AI buildouts is power and transmission infrastructure.
key_facts.excerpt: TeraWulf (NASDAQ: WULF) shares rose about 8% in pre-market trading on Tuesday... He added that the constraint is 'power... transmission infrastructure.'

stories.headline: Stord raises $250M at $3B valuation and launches robotics lab to challenge Amazon

key_facts.fact: Atlanta-based logistics startup Stord announced on May 26 a $250 million Series F funding round at a $3 billion valuation, led by existing investors.
key_facts.excerpt: Stord today announced a $250 million Series F funding round at a $3 billion valuation, led by existing investors doubling down on the company's accelerating growth.

key_facts.fact: The round included Strike Capital, Kleiner Perkins, Founders Fund, Franklin Templeton, Baillie Gifford, G Squared, Bond and Lux.
key_facts.excerpt: The round included Strike Capital, Kleiner Perkins, Founders Fund, Franklin Templeton, Baillie Gifford, G Squared, Bond, and Lux, among others.

key_facts.fact: Alongside the raise, Stord launched Stord Labs, a physical-AI and robotics lab at its Atlanta headquarters to develop robotics, agentic AI and automation for deployment across nearly 100 fulfillment facilities.
key_facts.excerpt: Stord announced Stord Labs, its dedicated environment for advancing physical AI and robotics... before deploying proven innovations across nearly 100 facilities immediately.

key_facts.fact: Stord reports 10x revenue growth and more than $15 billion of GMV across over 1,000 customers.
key_facts.excerpt: With 10x revenue growth and the trust of over $15B of GMV across more than 1,000 customers.

key_facts.fact: The company is positioning itself to challenge Amazon's e-commerce and fulfillment network, aiming to let independent brands deliver experiences that 'surpass Prime.'
key_facts.excerpt: launched a new physical AI and robotics lab in Atlanta to go up against Amazon's e-commerce and fulfillment network.

stories.headline: Human Archive raises $8.2M to train robots on first-person video from India's gig workers

key_facts.fact: Silicon Valley startup Human Archive said Tuesday, May 26 that it raised $8.2 million from Wing Venture Capital, NVP Capital, Y Combinator, and angels from OpenAI, Nvidia, Google, Meta, Mercor, AfterQuery, BAIR and SAIL.
key_facts.excerpt: Human Archive said Tuesday it has raised $8.2 million in funding from Wing Venture Capital, NVP Capital, Y Combinator, and angels from OpenAI, Nvidia, Google, Mercor, AfterQuery, BAIR, SAIL, Brad Boa, and Meta.

key_facts.fact: The company partners with India's home-services, hotel and restaurant firms to have workers wear camera caps that collect first-person (egocentric) video to train robots; it has more than 1,000 active headsets deployed.
key_facts.excerpt: partnering with these companies to have workers wear special caps with cameras to collect egocentric (first-person point of view) video data... it has more than 1,000 active headsets deployed across multiple locations.

key_facts.fact: Human Archive uses custom hardware - tactile gloves, full-body motion-capture suits and wrist cameras - synchronized with RGB-D data, and has more than 50 devices and over seven hardware products deployed.
key_facts.excerpt: additional devices, such as tactile gloves, a full-body motion capture suit, and wrist cameras... synchronously aligned with RGB-D... It already has more than 50 different devices deployed... more than seven different hardware products.

key_facts.fact: The company pays workers a base rate of $1 per hour for participating in data collection.
key_facts.excerpt: The company pays workers a base rate of $1 per hour for participating in egocentric data collection.

key_facts.fact: Human Archive was founded by four UC Berkeley and Stanford students - Samay Maini, Rushil Agarwal, Shloke Patel, and CEO Raj Patel.
key_facts.excerpt: founded by three students from UC Berkeley and one from Stanford - Samay Maini, Rushil Agarwal, Shloke Patel, and Raj Patel... (Raj Patel is CEO.)

key_facts.fact: The bet targets a key bottleneck for physical AI: a shortage of high-quality, real-world data showing humans doing everyday work.
key_facts.excerpt: they face a critical bottleneck - a shortage of high-quality, real-world training data showing humans doing everyday work.

key_facts.fact: India's Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) is looking into the consent mechanisms and data-collection practices of startups gathering egocentric data via home-service workers.
key_facts.excerpt: India's Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology is looking into the consent mechanisms and data-collection practices of startups collecting egocentric data through home service workers.

sources.title: This startup is betting India's gig economy can train the world's robots
